title: Healthcare Checklist (29 CFR 1910.502)
subtitle: Use when inspecting a covered healthcare setting or reviewing its COVID-19 program.
instructions: Mark every item OK, Defect or N/A.
For each Defect, record the location and the fix needed, tell the COVID-19 safety coordinator, and recheck once it is corrected.
Your COVID-19 plan, manufacturers' instructions and site rules may add checks.

sections.title: COVID-19 plan, coordinator and hazard assessment
items: A current plan exists for this workplace, or a workplace-type plan that includes this site's specific information.
The plan is in writing where the employer has over 10 employees.
At least one COVID-19 safety coordinator is designated, knows infection control for this workplace and has authority to enforce the plan.
The written plan states who the safety coordinator(s) are.
A workplace-specific assessment identifying COVID-19 hazards is on file.
Where fully vaccinated employees are exempted from controls in a well-defined area, the plan includes procedures to determine vaccination status.
Records show non-managerial employees and their representatives, if any, were asked for input on the assessment and the plan.
There is evidence the plan's effectiveness is monitored and the plan is updated when needed.

sections.title: Patient screening, PPE and aerosol-generating procedures
items: Entry points to the patient care setting are limited and monitored.
Every patient, resident, client, delivery person and other visitor is screened and triaged on entry.
Employees wear facemasks over nose and mouth indoors and in shared work vehicles, apart from the exceptions in 1910.502(f)(1)(iii).
Enough facemasks are on hand for changes at least once per day and whenever soiled or damaged.
Required face shields are cleaned daily and show no damage.
Staff exposed to confirmed or suspected COVID-19 patients have respirators issued and worn as 1910.134 requires.
The same staff wear gloves, eye protection and an isolation gown or other protective clothing.
Only employees essential to patient care and procedure support are in the room during aerosol-generating procedures on patients with known or suspected COVID-19.
Those procedures take place in an existing AIIR when one is available.
Surfaces and equipment in the room or area are cleaned and disinfected after each such procedure.

sections.title: Distancing, barriers, cleaning and ventilation
items: Employees are kept 6 feet or more from others indoors, except in activities shown to be infeasible, such as hands-on care, or momentary passing.
Cleanable or disposable solid barriers are in place at fixed lobby, check-in, triage, pharmacy window and bill payment stations where people are closer than 6 feet, unless shown infeasible.
Barriers block the face-to-face pathway between people where they normally stand or sit.
Outside patient care areas and resident rooms, high-touch surfaces and equipment are cleaned at least once a day, with cleaners applied as the manufacturer directs.
Alcohol-based hand rub with at least 60% alcohol, or readily accessible hand washing facilities, is available.
Filters are MERV 13 or higher, or the highest efficiency compatible with the HVAC system.
Filters are maintained and replaced when needed for proper HVAC performance.
Intake ports are clean, maintained and clear of debris.
Any existing AIIR is maintained and operated to its design and construction criteria.

sections.title: Employee screening, notification and removal
items: Each employee is screened before every work day and shift, by self-monitoring or in person.
Any test the employer requires for screening is provided free to employees.

Employees have been told to report promptly a positive test or diagnosis, a provider's suspicion of COVID-19, unexplained loss of taste or smell, or fever (≥100.4 °F) with new unexplained cough and shortness of breath.
Records show close contacts without a respirator and required PPE were told, with contact dates, no more than 24 hours after the employer was notified of a positive case.
Exposure notices contain no employee names, contact details or occupations.
Employees known to be COVID-19 positive are removed at once and kept away until cleared under 1910.502(l)(6).
Where the employer is not exempt under 1910.502(l)(5)(i), removed employees keep their benefits and regular pay up to $1,400 per week, subject to the reduction in 1910.502(l)(5)(iii)(B).
Employees get reasonable time and paid leave for vaccination and any side effects.

sections.title: Training, worker rights and records
items: Each employee has been trained in a language and at a literacy level they understand, on the topics in 1910.502(n)(1).
Training is run or overseen by someone knowledgeable in the subject as it relates to the job.
Trainees can ask questions and get answers from a knowledgeable person during training.
Employees have been told of their right to the standard's protections and the ban on retaliation.
All past and current versions of the plan are retained.
Each entry has the name, one contact method, occupation, work location, last day on site, test or diagnosis date, and first symptom date if any.
Entries are made no later than 24 hours after the employer learns of a positive case.
The log is kept as a confidential medical record and disclosed only as the ETS or other federal law requires.
A procedure exists for telling OSHA of each work-related COVID-19 fatality within 8 hours of learning of it.
A procedure exists for telling OSHA of each work-related COVID-19 in-patient hospitalization inside 24 hours.

disclaimer: General guidance only, not legal advice. Check the current regulation and your employer's procedures.
